candidate.title: BLESS
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina BLESS schematic: in situ proximal-linker labeling of existing DNA double-strand ends, DNA isolation/fragmentation, streptavidin enrichment, distal-linker addition, and the combined I-SceI/PCR block ending in enriched DNA. The far-left DSB icon identifies the target rather than a depicted break-induction step. The primary 2013 BLESS paper resolves linker identity, attachment and readout; its HaeIII fragmentation is distinguished from the drawing’s “random shearing”. Sequencing explains the intended readout but is not an additional drawn operation, and platform-specific library finishing is outside the depicted endpoint.

states.label: Genome DNA containing accessible double-strand ends
features: Blue duplex genomic DNA with an existing double-strand discontinuity; no nuclease induction is depicted.
The paper places the first ligation in purified nuclei from fixed cells, before genomic DNA extraction; blunted, 5′-phosphorylated ends are the ligation substrate.

operations.label: Ligate primer
operations.description: Ligate the biotinylated proximal linker to accessible genomic double-strand ends in situ, changing untagged genomic DNA to DNA with a covalent capture handle and a junction-marking linker. The source calls this reagent a primer; the primary paper identifies a ligated hairpin linker.
operations.mechanism: Primary BLESS uses T4 DNA ligase on blunted, 5′-phosphorylated DSB ends in purified nuclei. Biotin is carried by the proximal linker.
operations.information_effect: Encodes the labeled end physically as the junction between a defined proximal barcode and adjacent genomic DNA. Labeling precedes extraction, helping distinguish those ends from new fragmentation boundaries; this does not imply perfect specificity.

operations.label: DNA isolation and random shearing
operations.description: Extract the proximally labeled genomic DNA and fragment it into a mixture containing marked break-adjacent pieces and unmarked genomic pieces. Preserve the diagram’s random-shearing label at schematic scope; the inspected 2013 implementation instead used HaeIII digestion for fragmentation (c_fragmentation).
operations.mechanism: Isolation followed by fragmentation is shown as a single broad block. The original-paper fragmentation mechanism is HaeIII restriction digestion; random mechanical shearing is not attributed to that implementation.
operations.information_effect: Separates genomic material into shorter pieces while retaining the proximal mark on the piece adjacent to each labeled end. The opposite end of that piece is fragmentation-derived and does not itself identify another biological DSB.

operations.label: Capture on streptavidin beads
operations.description: Bind biotin-bearing, proximally labeled genomic fragments to streptavidin beads, enriching them relative to the unmarked fragments depicted as faded free DNA.
operations.mechanism: Affinity capture through linker biotin and streptavidin; bead binding changes attachment and population composition rather than genomic sequence.
operations.information_effect: Retains the genomic-insert/proximal-linker association in a bead-bound population. This is a chemical enrichment of tagged material and does not by itself prove that every recovered molecule is a biological DSB.

operations.label: Distal primer
operations.description: Ligate the distal linker to the free fragmentation-derived end of the captured genomic fragment, producing a genomic insert bracketed by distinct proximal and distal linkers. The bead is absent from the drawing of the resulting intermediate, but the paper places this ligation on the captured material before release.
operations.mechanism: T4-ligase-mediated distal-linker attachment on beads is established by the primary paper; the green hairpin icon is a ligated linker reagent rather than a separate amplification reaction.
operations.information_effect: Adds the second known sequence interface needed for PCR and sequencing, while the proximal side retains the labeled-break association and the distal side identifies the other library boundary.

operations.label: Digest with I-SceI and PCR
operations.description: Digest the linker structures to release captured fragments, then amplify released fragments using linker-specific PCR primers. These consecutive transformations remain one operation because the Illumina drawing combines them in a single caption and supplies no intervening material boundary. The resulting blue DNA represents enriched genomic amplicons.
operations.mechanism: I-SceI acts on the linker recognition sites; PCR amplifies released genomic fragments through the known linker interfaces. The nuclease and PCR machinery are reagents, not target DNA.
operations.information_effect: Produces sufficient copies of labeled break-adjacent genomic DNA for sequencing. Barcode-adjacent genomic sequence can locate the end that was labeled at nucleotide resolution, rather than infer it from a distal fragmentation boundary. End resection can displace that labeled boundary from the original cleavage site. Only accessible unjoined ends present at sampling are represented, with reported background and fixation limitations.

method_scopes.rationale: The card heading, matching collection-page heading and “A schematic overview of BLESS” caption establish BLESS as the only target. Its expanded name is an alias. All five local operations belong to the illustrated BLESS route, clarified by the original primary workflow; hairpin linker terminology and the HaeIII-versus-shearing distinction do not introduce another named method. LAM-HTGTS and GUIDE-seq papers supply comparison/limitation evidence, and the SaCas9 study is an application. None is a depicted alternative. TruSeq Nano is a catalogue kit association, not an additional depicted library-preparation operation.
